question: Under which of the following Acts were the commercial activities to be taken care by the East India Company and the political activities by the British parliament?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Pitts India Act, 1784**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Pitts India Act of 1784, also known as the East India Company Act, was introduced to address the administrative and political issues related to British territories in India.
 
• This Act distinguished between the commercial and political activities of the East India Company and brought the political functions under the control of the British government.
 
• The Act established a Board of Control to oversee the political affairs of the Company, while the Court of Directors managed its commercial activities.
 
• It marked the beginning of the dual system of governance, with the British Crown and the East India Company sharing administrative responsibilities.
 
• The Act was significant in consolidating British control over India and laid the groundwork for future legislative and administrative reforms.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Regulating Act of 1773**

 
 
• This was the first act to regulate the affairs of the East India Company.
 
• It established a system of government for the British territories in India, including the post of Governor-General of Bengal.
 
• The Act aimed to address the issues of corruption and mismanagement within the Company.
 
 
 
• **Government of India Act 1858**
 
 
• Following the Indian Rebellion of 1857, this Act transferred the administration of India from the East India Company to the British Crown.
 
• A new office called the Secretary of State for India was created to oversee Indian affairs.
 
• The Act marked the end of the Company rule and the beginning of the British Raj.
 
 
 
• **Indian Councils Act 1861**
 
 
• This Act introduced a representative element into the governance of India.
 
• It allowed for the inclusion of Indian members in the legislative councils.
 
• It aimed to involve Indians in the process of law-making and administration.
 
 
 
• **Government of India Act 1935**
 
 
• This was the longest act enacted by the British Parliament for governing India.
 
• It proposed the establishment of an All India Federation and introduced provincial autonomy.
 
• The Act laid the foundation for the constitutional structure of independent India.
